Hey everybody! First time engaging the community about anything. I'm here to talk about my squats!

I'm 28m, using the Stronglifs 5x5 app, and I've been at it for like six months. I'd been using the free bars for everything, but I was concerned about my squats. A little investigation revealed that my form was pretty terrible. I was throwing my ass back whenever I hit the sticking point, and then just going into a longer and longer 'good morning' lift.

So, I switched over to the smith press for my squats and I dropped about 60lbs off (from 230lbs to 170lbs), and it's been amazing! I've learned much more about tightening my shoulders, positioning the bar, and I can really hit that sticking point and push through and know that I'm overcoming the right forces with the right muscles. Last workout, I moved back to a free bar because a gym trainer was using the smith with a newb, and things were much better, but I could feel my ass kicking out and my shoulders going forward toward the end of my fourth and fifth sets.

Am I missing out on anything by sticking with the smith press? Should I try to make a transition back to the bar, and if so, how should I go about it?
Should I be aiming to switch off the smith press for squats?

You should definitely try to transition back to bar. I am not a smith machine hater, I am really not. It was very useful for me to help figure out my form, and it obviously taught you a lot. However, because it controls the dimensions the bar can move on, you lose the muscle activation that comes with stabilizing the bar yourself to move it up and down with proper form. You deloaded, you learned your motions for the squat, so now its time to remove the "training wheels" so to speak. If your ass was kicking out and your shoulders were going forward going back to free weights, you just have to deload again and work at it.

Yeah, this makes sense. Update, since I've gone back to the bar (and deloaded again), I've been feeling like I have much better control over my form and I think I have a decent handle on it. Thanks for the advice!
